settings.heading: Your K-beauty routine, step by step
settings.text: K-beauty isn't a shelf full of products. It's a ritual: gentle formulas, thin layers, and a few minutes for you, every day.

settings.heading: Why island skin loves it
settings.text: It was made for heat and humidity, which is island life in a sentence. Sun, salt and aircon wear your skin barrier down. This routine is all about building it back.

settings.heading: The routine
settings.text: Morning and night, in this order. Thin layers, patted in, a few seconds between each.
settings.evening_text: At night, the same order without sunscreen. Thin layers, patted in, a few seconds between each.

settings.name: Cleanse
settings.text: Start clean. A gentle, low-foam cleanser takes off sunscreen, salt and the whole day without stripping your skin, so it doesn't feel tight and then turn oily.

settings.name: Tone
settings.text: Forget the alcohol splash you remember. A Korean toner is a thin layer of water and calming plant extracts that puts moisture back and preps your skin for everything after it.

settings.name: Treat
settings.text: This is the step that does the heavy lifting. Pick a serum for one job: hydrate, brighten or calm. Island skin? Start with hydration.

settings.name: Moisturise
settings.text: Seal it all in. A cream looks after the skin barrier that sun, salt and aircon wear down. Go light in the morning and richer at night.

settings.name: Protect
settings.text: Sunscreen every morning, rain or shine, indoors or out. If you only do one step, make it this one.

settings.heading: Start with three steps, not five
settings.text: Cleanse, tone, protect. Do that for a month, then add a serum and a cream when you're ready.

settings.heading: The real formula, or nothing
settings.text:
A lot of K-beauty in Mauritius arrives in a suitcase, or through someone who can't say where it was kept, for how long, or whether it's the real thing.

We're here to change that. Every product shows its full ingredient list, so you can check it against the brand's own. And if you have a question, just ask.
